To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the bipolar hybrid of mCP--Ph-SiPh3:FIpic has a superior thermal stability compared to that of mCP: SiPh4:FIpic.

thermal annealing of the emitting layers in PhOLEDs can cause phase transformation in the emitting layers and that the resulting crystallization or pinhole creation diminishes the PhOLED's performance and stability.

(i) the thermal stability of PhOLEDs is strongly affected by the presence of a glassy top layer; (ii) crystallization of the EMLs is a major cause of PhOLED degradation; (iii) crystallization of PhOLED EMLs can be prevented by using a bipolar host that is a hybrid of a glass-forming and an oligomeric host.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the temporal stability of PhOLED devices with a bipolar hybrid EML and its dependence on the thermal annealing conditions of the emitting layer.
the thermal stability of PhOLEDs and the effect of thermal annealing on the PhOLED performance.
the stability of blue PhOLEDs under thermal stress.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
annealing the emitting layers at temperatures below their Tg for durations below the onset of crystallization or pinhole generation is a viable approach to improve PhOLED performance and stability.
the thermal stability of PhOLEDs is not only determined by the Tg of the EML but also by the Tg and the thermal stability of the hole transport layer.

annealing of mCPPhSiPh4:FiPic at 60 ° C for 1 hour led to about 40% loss of EQE, while the pristine device's performance was maintained with mCPPhSiPH3:FiPic annealed at 100 ° C for 24 hours, beyond which other factors began to affect device performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the bipolarity in the hybrid materials can be used to mitigate morphological instability in PhOLEDs, and that the hybrid bipolarity is more robust in preventing morphological instability than the bipolarity of the host material alone.
bipolar hybrids with the glassy TmPVPB layer are more robust to morphological instability than bipolar hybrids without it.

annealing of the EML at temperatures below the Tg of the EML can improve device performance, but annealing at temperatures above the Tg can cause morphological instabilities and performance deterioration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PhOLED lifetime is not only determined by the stability of the EMLs.
thermal annealing of the emitting layer in PhOLEDs is a double-edged sword.
the PhOLED lifetime can be improved by annealing mCP--Ph-SiPh3:FIrpic at 60 ° C for up to 1 h.
